summary.title: Night noise from the upstairs flat
summary.what_happened: My upstairs neighbours have a newborn who cries at night. On weekends they play loud music until 2am. The building rules say quiet hours are 22:00 to 07:00. I have banged on the ceiling with a broom a few times. I have not spoken to them directly.
summary.my_feelings: I am exhausted. I work early shifts.
summary.my_needs: I need to be able to sleep at night.
summary.desired_outcome: I want both the music and the crying to stop at night.

consult.text:
Being woken at night when you start work early is draining, and it makes sense that you are worn out. Your concern about the weekend music until 2am looks reasonable, especially with quiet hours from 22:00 to 07:00.

Your neighbours may see this differently. A newborn cries at any hour and parents often cannot stop it. They may be just as tired as you are. They may also have no idea the music or the crying reaches you, because nobody has told them.

One thing that may have made this harder is that banging on the ceiling is the only message they have had so far. Without a conversation, they may find it hostile, or not understand what it means.

We do not know whether they realise how much sound carries, or how they would respond if you spoke to them calmly.

Some next steps. First, consider a short, friendly note or conversation that names the music specifically, since that is something they can change. Second, ask whether there is anything that would help them with the night noise, such as when it is worst. Third, find out what your building's process is if talking does not work.
Babies crying is still noise. Why should I put up with it just because it's a baby?

It sounds like you are very tired and tired of being asked to put up with things. That feeling is fair. A crying baby is noise, and it does affect your sleep.

The difference I would point to is that parents of a newborn cannot fully control the crying, while loud music until 2am is a choice they can change. That is why I would keep those two things apart when you talk to them. Asking for the music to stop is a clear, reasonable request. For the crying, it may help more to tell them how it affects you and ask what could be done, rather than expect it to stop.

So far they have only heard banging, not your words. A calm first conversation gives you the best chance of getting the music turned down.

You could start with the draft below, which focuses on the music and lets them know how the night noise affects you.

share_draft: Hi, I live in the flat below you. I wanted to talk to you directly, because so far I have only banged on the ceiling a few times, and I realise that was not a helpful way to tell you. I work early shifts, and lately I have not been sleeping well because of noise at night. On weekends the music has gone on until about 2am, and I would like to ask if it could be turned down after 22:00, which is when the building's quiet hours start. I also hear a baby at night, and I know that is hard to control. I would like to find something that works for both of us. How do things look from your side?
